```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab03", title = "Autocorrelation")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "A white-noise ACF should look roughly:",
  q2 = "Beer ACF typically shows strong spikes near which seasonal lag (quarterly data)?",
  q3 = "Name three differences between the Beer ACF and a white-noise ACF."
)
```

## What you will do

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `learnr`, `fpp3`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

## Beer ACF
```{r beer-acf, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
library(fpp3)
aus_production |> autoplot(Beer)
aus_production |> ACF(Beer) |> autoplot()
```

## White noise null
```{r wn-acf, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=5}
set.seed(1)
wn <- tsibble(t = 1:200, y = rnorm(200), index = t)
wn |> gg_acf(y)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("Near zero for lags > 0 (within noise bands)", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Slow geometric decay forever"),
  answer("A single spike only at lag 100"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Lag 4 (and multiples)", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Lag 1 only"),
  answer("Lag 12 only"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "1) … 2) … 3) …",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Answer the questions above first, type your name, download the `.txt`, and upload it.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
